title: Ranveer Singh Sued FWICE. A Veteran Producer Sued Them Too. The Don 3 Mess Is Now Officially a Court Fight.
excerpt: A non-cooperation directive, a ₹45 crore claim, legal notices flying in both directions, and a Bombay Civil Court petition that could reshape how Bollywood resolves its disputes.
body:
The Don 3 dispute between Ranveer Singh and Farhan Akhtar's Excel Entertainment has become the most consequential labor fight in contemporary Bollywood. What started as a casting disagreement has now landed in Bombay Civil Court, with legal notices flying from multiple directions and the Federation of Western India Cine Employees caught in the crossfire.

How It Got Here

The timeline is straightforward but the fallout has been anything but. Ranveer Singh exited Don 3 — the highly anticipated continuation of the franchise that Shah Rukh Khan made iconic — after significant pre-production work had already been completed. Excel Entertainment, led by Farhan Akhtar and Ritesh Sidhwani, claimed the withdrawal caused financial losses of ₹45 crore. They approached FWICE for intervention.

On May 25, FWICE escalated. The federation issued a non-cooperation directive against Ranveer, effectively urging its affiliated workers and technicians to refuse work with the actor until the dispute was resolved. FWICE President Ashoke Pandit told reporters the organization had sent multiple notices to Ranveer but received no response. He later clarified the directive was not a "ban" — the federation lacks the legal authority to impose one — but the practical effect was the same. If crews refuse to work with you, you cannot make films.

The Legal Counterattack

Ranveer's camp responded in the courts. According to reports, the actor served a legal notice to FWICE challenging the legitimacy of the directive and its impact on his professional commitments. His spokesperson released a measured statement: "While various narratives and speculations have emerged over time, Ranveer has never felt it necessary to respond publicly or engage in speculation. His focus remains steadfast on his work and future commitments."

But the more structurally significant legal move came from an unexpected quarter. Veteran producer T.P. Aggarwal — who served as President of the Indian Motion Picture Producers' Association for 17 years and was elected President of the Film Federation of India four times — filed a petition in the Bombay Civil Court at Dindoshi against both FWICE and IMPPA. His argument is sweeping: no individual or organization has the legal authority to impose a ban or issue a non-cooperation directive against members of the film industry.

"The film industry thrives on collaboration, and it is important that matters of this nature are addressed through proper legal and professional channels," Aggarwal said in a statement. "Any attempt to discourage people from working with an individual should not be taken lightly. Such actions can have far-reaching consequences for livelihoods and creative freedom."

Court notices have been served to both FWICE and IMPPA as of June 1.

What Today Might Bring

Bollywood Hungama has reported that FWICE is likely to announce the lifting of the non-cooperation directive at a press conference scheduled for today, June 3. Sources suggest the revocation has been done in consultation with senior industry members. If confirmed, the immediate standoff ends — but the court petition from Aggarwal raises questions that won't disappear with a press conference.

Why This Matters for the Diaspora

For NRIs who follow Bollywood, the Don franchise carries particular significance. It's one of the few Hindi film series with genuine global name recognition, and its future now hinges on a legal dispute over creative commitments and financial accountability. The Aggarwal petition, if it results in a favorable precedent, could fundamentally change how Bollywood resolves disputes between talent and producers — moving from union pressure campaigns to formal legal channels.

Ranveer, meanwhile, is not short of work. His Dhurandhar 2: The Revenge — which grossed ₹1,800 crore worldwide — hits JioHotstar on June 4. But the Don 3 cloud will follow him until the courts have their say, and the franchise itself remains in limbo, waiting for either a resolution or a recast.

The irony isn't lost on anyone: the actor who replaced Shah Rukh Khan in the Don chair is now at the center of a controversy about what it means to walk away from a franchise that doesn't want to let go.
